Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0053", "row_sha256": "a17f05ae1aa85d0665851f0d0eb3ceef9c0c6a8faa192508d883ff5923634f5e", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need a prompt cleaned up for a shift at North Quay Community Kitchen this thursday. it’s the evening service, 5:30 to 7:00, and we’re expecting about 40 guests. the kitchen has two labeled tubs of lentil soup, L-17 and L-18, 12 litres in each. the opening refrigerator log is on the clipboard by the pantry door. i haven’t checked yet whether the entries meet the condition, so make that the switch between the two possible tasks, not a detail to gloss over.

if the log has an entry for both tubs for every check at 2:00, 3:00, and 4:00 p.m., and every recorded temperature is at or below 5°C, then ask for a practical staffing and service plan for the 5:30–7:00 soup service. all six entries need to be present; one missing entry means the condition does not hold. the plan is the main task, but only under that condition. it should use the actual staff and equipment below and fit the service window. don’t turn the condition into a general statement that the soup has been checked, because the exact readings and complete set of entries are what decide which task to do.

if the condition doesn’t hold for any reason, do not make the service plan. instead, ask for a short handoff note to the shift coordinator, Omar, that identifies the relevant tub or tubs and the missing entry or recorded temperature that failed the stated test. ask the note to say that the log needs follow-up before a service plan is made. this is the alternative, not an extra section to attach to a plan. don’t ask the writer to decide whether the soup can be served or to say it is unsafe; the log test is only the condition for choosing the requested output.

for the plan case, the people available are Mina, the shift lead; Priya, who can portion soup; Joel, who can manage the serving table; and Ben, who is assigned to the wash station. a fifth volunteer is expected at 5:15 but we don’t know their name or what they can do, so don’t build the plan around a skill or responsibility we haven’t given them. Mina needs to stay available to coordinate the kitchen rather than being treated as an extra person at every station. there are two working burners, one soup ladle, and one wheeled service cart. please make a usable sequence of jobs, but don’t invent extra equipment or staff.

some other service details: six dining tables are already set, and the soup line forms beside the blue noticeboard near the east entrance. bread is set out separately. the serving card for this soup says “vegetarian” and notes lentils and celery. there isn’t another ingredient or allergen sheet in the information i have, so don’t add claims about ingredients. Mina said, “Please keep the entrance clear for the pantry line; the soup queue turns beside the blue noticeboard.” the east entrance is also the route pantry guests use, so the plan should account for that practical space issue without moving the queue to a place we haven’t named.

make the plan concrete enough to help during the shift, not a broad description of how kitchens work. include a short timeline from before 5:30 through the end of service at 7:00, with staff roles linked to the tasks they can actually do. it’s useful to show when the soup is brought to the table and how the serving and wash areas fit together, but don’t assume a serving temperature, a replenishment amount, or a new food-handling rule; none was supplied. we need a clear arrangement for serving 40 guests from the two tubs, but we haven’t specified a number of bowls per tub or the size of a portion.

1. the output should be one of two things, chosen strictly from the refrigerator-log test above: the staffing and service plan when every required entry is present and at or below 5°C, or the handoff note when that test fails. keep the two outputs mutually exclusive. the note should be directed to Omar and state the log issue plainly; the plan should cover the actual service window and available team. neither output should invent what the log says.

please preserve the tub labels L-17 and L-18, the times, the temperature threshold, the kitchen name, and the distinction between the main task and the fallback. the plan can use concise sections or bullets if that makes it readable during a shift. don’t add an introduction, explanation of your choices, or a summary after the requested document. return only the applicable document. the final wording should feel like a practical kitchen prompt for this one thursday, not a standing policy for future shifts.", "output": "Write one practical document for this Thursday’s evening service at North Quay Community Kitchen, scheduled from 5:30 to 7:00 p.m. About 40 guests are expected. Two labeled tubs of lentil soup, L-17 and L-18, contain 12 litres each. The opening refrigerator log is on the clipboard by the pantry door. I have not yet checked whether its entries meet the condition below, so use the log test to choose the requested document.

**Choose exactly one task:**

- **If the condition holds:** The log contains an entry for each tub at 2:00, 3:00, and 4:00 p.m. (all six entries are present), and every recorded temperature is at or below 5°C. Create a practical staffing and service plan for the 5:30–7:00 soup service.
- **If the condition does not hold:** Do not create a service plan. Write a short handoff note to shift coordinator Omar that identifies the affected tub or tubs and the missing entry or recorded temperature that failed the test. State that the log needs follow-up before a service plan is made. This note is the alternative, not an additional section to a plan. Do not decide whether the soup can be served or say that it is unsafe; the log test only determines which document to produce.

For the service plan, use only the available staff and equipment. Mina is the shift lead and needs to remain available to coordinate the kitchen, rather than being assigned as extra staff at every station. Priya can portion soup, Joel can manage the serving table, and Ben is assigned to the wash station. A fifth volunteer is expected at 5:15, but their name and skills are unknown; do not assign them an unprovided skill or responsibility. The kitchen has two working burners, one soup ladle, and one wheeled service cart. Do not invent additional staff or equipment.

Six dining tables are already set. The soup line forms beside the blue noticeboard near the east entrance, which is also used by pantry guests. Mina said, “Please keep the entrance clear for the pantry line; the soup queue turns beside the blue noticeboard.” Account for this space issue without moving the queue to an unspecified location. Bread is set out separately. The soup’s serving card says “vegetarian” and notes lentils and celery. No other ingredient or allergen information has been supplied, so do not add claims about ingredients.

If the log test permits a plan, make it useful during the shift rather than a general description of kitchen work. Include a concise timeline from before 5:30 through the end of service at 7:00, with roles matched to the tasks each person can do. Show when the soup is brought to the table and how the serving and wash areas fit together. Do not assume a serving temperature, replenishment amount, portion size, number of bowls per tub, or additional food-handling rule; none has been provided. The plan should address serving 40 guests from the two tubs without inventing those details.

Keep the two possible outputs mutually exclusive. Preserve the kitchen name, tub labels L-17 and L-18, times, temperature threshold, and the distinction between the main task and the fallback. Use concise sections or bullets if helpful. Return only the applicable document, with no introduction, explanation of your choices, or summary. Make the wording practical for this one Thursday, not a standing policy for future shifts."}]
